Count histories of many species at once

Source: R/07_count_history.R
pam_count_histories.Rd

Builds a pam_count_history() for every species (or the species you name) in one pass over the detections. All histories share the same sites, occasions, effort and site covariates, which is what multi-species models need.

Usage

pam_count_histories(
  cfg,
  species = NULL,
  run_id = cfg$birdnet$run_id,
  bin_days = NULL,
  count = c("events", "files"),
  thresholds = NULL,
  min_effort_hours = NULL,
  site_covariates = NULL,
  min_total = 1
)

Arguments

cfg

A pam_config object.

species

Optional species to include: scientific names, common names or species labels (any capitalisation). NULL (the default) takes every species in the detections.

run_id

Detection run (sub-folder of paths$detections).

bin_days

Length of an occasion in days. NULL uses occupancy$occasion_length_days (1 if not set).

count

What to count: "events" (the default; detected events, which Stage 4 forms by merging overlapping BirdNET windows) or "files" (the number of recordings with at least one detection, which cannot exceed the number of recordings and is less affected by one animal calling for a long time).

thresholds

Optional per-species thresholds (a data frame, or the path of a CSV file, with scientific_name and threshold), for example from pam_species_thresholds().

min_effort_hours

Minimum recorded hours for an occasion to count as surveyed; others are NA. NULL uses occupancy$min_effort_hours (2 if not set).

site_covariates

Optional data frame of site covariates with a site_id column (for example habitat or elevation). Every site must have a row.

min_total

Species with fewer than this many counts in total, over all sites and occasions, are left out (default 1, which drops species with no count after the thresholds).

Value

An object of class pam_count_histories: a named list (one pam_count_history() per species, named by species label).

Details

Pass the result to pam_model_input() to get a species by site by occasion array for multi-species models, or take one species with histories[["label"]].

See also

pam_count_history(), pam_model_input()

Examples

ex <- pam_example_project()
# the later stages read the master table that the scan builds
res <- suppressMessages(pam_scan_audio(ex$cfg))
proc <- suppressMessages(pam_process_detections(ex$cfg))
hists <- suppressMessages(pam_count_histories(ex$cfg))
names(hists)
#> [1] "Ducula nicobarica_Nicobar Imperial-Pigeon" 
#> [2] "Gracula religiosa_Common Hill Myna"        
#> [3] "Psittacula longicauda_Long-tailed Parakeet"
